name: Prestosuchus
currentFacts: It was a large apex predator.
It had an upright limb posture.
Closely related to early crocodilians.

name: Batrachotomus
currentFacts: Preyed on giant amphibians.
It was a heavily built rauisuchian.
Walked on four legs but could rear up.

name: Ornithosuchus
currentFacts: It had a distinctive crocodile-like ankle.
Known for its 'bird crocodile' skull shape.
Exhibited facultative bipedalism.

name: Smilosuchus
currentFacts: Had a heavy, robust snout.
Possessed a large cranial crest.
An apex predator in aquatic environments.

name: Phytosaurus
currentFacts: Name translates to 'plant reptile' due to mistaken tooth interpretation.
Actually a carnivorous aquatic predator.
Gave its name to the entire group of phytosaurs.

name: Machaeroprosopus
currentFacts: Had a long, narrow snout for catching fish.
Lived in widespread river systems.
Its fossils are excellent biostratigraphic markers.

name: Leptosuchus
currentFacts: Possessed a relatively broad skull.
Armored with bony scutes.
A widespread Late Triassic predator.

name: Redondasaurus
currentFacts: Very advanced phytosaur species.
Highly adapted for aquatic ambush.
Survived until the end-Triassic extinction event.

name: Mystriosuchus
currentFacts: Highly adapted for marine life.
Snout was extremely elongated.
Some specimens found in full marine deposits.

name: Stagonolepis
currentFacts: Had a pig-like rooting snout.
Body was heavily encased in rectangular scutes.
One of the best-understood early aetosaurs.

name: Aetosaurus
currentFacts: One of the smallest known aetosaurs.
May have exhibited gregarious behavior.
Name means 'eagle lizard'.

name: Neoaetosauroides
currentFacts: Possessed teeth adapted for a soft diet or omnivory.
Had distinctively long limbs.
First aetosaur with well-preserved limb elements.

name: Longosuchus
currentFacts: Had large curved spikes on its shoulders.
A relatively robust and slow-moving aetosaur.
Common in Late Triassic fossil assemblages.

name: Gracilisuchus
currentFacts: A very small, agile pseudosuchian.
Walked primarily on its hind legs.
Had a double row of scutes along its back.

name: Erpetosuchus
currentFacts: Very small archosaur.
Had a specialized skull suggesting an insectivorous diet.
Shares features with early crocodilians.

name: Saltoposuchus
currentFacts: Name translates to 'leaping crocodile'.
Very lightly built and bipedal.
Covered with thin, elongated scutes.

name: Terrestrisuchus
currentFacts: Extremely slender, greyhound-like proportions.
A fully terrestrial early crocodylomorph.
Very small, measuring around half a meter in length.

name: Hesperosuchus
currentFacts: Agile terrestrial predator.
Had distinctively long hind legs.
Likely preyed on large insects and small vertebrates.

name: Sphenosuchus
currentFacts: A primitive crocodylomorph with a somewhat dog-like stance.
Had a highly specialized quadrate bone.
Fully terrestrial and fast-running.

name: Protosuchus
currentFacts: Had short, powerful jaws.
Represented a transition toward amphibious crocodyliforms.
Heavily armored with dorsal and ventral scutes.

name: Effigia
currentFacts: A remarkable example of convergent evolution with ornithomimid dinosaurs.
Completely toothless with a beak.
Bipedal and highly cursorial.

name: Shuvosaurus
currentFacts: Another beaked, toothless pseudosuchian.
Closely related to Effigia.
Demonstrates high diversity among Triassic archosaurs.

name: Lotosaurus
currentFacts: Possessed a prominent sail on its back.
Had a toothless, beaked mouth.
Believed to have been an herbivore.

name: Arizonasaurus
currentFacts: A sail-backed poposauroid.
Sail may have been used for thermoregulation or display.
Older than many other famous Triassic archosaurs.

name: Sillosuchus
currentFacts: A very large, bipedal predator.
Part of the unique South American Triassic fauna.
Had complex cervical vertebrae.

name: Sharovipteryx
currentFacts: Had gliding membranes primarily on its hind limbs.
The only known 'hind-winged' glider.
Likely a leaper from tree to tree.

name: Longisquama
currentFacts: Possessed incredibly long, feather-like dorsal scales.
Subject of intense debate regarding avian origins.
A highly unusual diapsid reptile.

name: Tanystropheus
currentFacts: Neck was longer than its body and tail combined.
Neck consisted of only 12 or 13 extremely elongated vertebrae.
Likely an ambush predator in shallow waters.

name: Macrocnemus
currentFacts: A terrestrial or semi-aquatic prolacertiform.
Had long, slender hind limbs for running.
Related to Tanystropheus but with a shorter neck.

name: Dinocephalosaurus
currentFacts: First archosauromorph known to give live birth.
Neck had over 25 vertebrae.
Fully marine and incapable of coming on land.

name: Placodus
currentFacts: Had thick, flat teeth for crushing shellfish.
Possessed heavy bones for ballast in water.
Looked somewhat like a marine iguana.

name: Cyamodus
currentFacts: Carried a broad, turtle-like carapace.
Carapace was divided into two distinct sections.
Bottom feeder specialized in hard-shelled prey.

name: Henodus
currentFacts: Possessed a very boxy, flat shell.
Had a single tooth on each side, relying mostly on a beak.
May have been a filter feeder.

name: Nothosaurus
currentFacts: A semi-oceanic predator with a long neck and tail.
Had webbed toes instead of fully formed flippers.
Probably lived similarly to modern seals.

name: Lariosaurus
currentFacts: One of the smallest nothosaurs.
Forelimbs were modified into flippers, but hindlimbs retained toes.
Likely inhabited shallow coastal lagoons.

name: Ceresiosaurus
currentFacts: A larger nothosaur with highly adapted flippers.
Excellent swimmer due to hyperphalangy in its digits.
A transitional form toward plesiosaurs.

name: Pistosaurus
currentFacts: Had a stiff spine and plesiosaur-like skull.
A key transitional fossil linking nothosaurs and plesiosaurs.
Fully marine, utilizing flipper-based locomotion.

name: Simosaurus
currentFacts: Had a blunt, short snout unlike other nothosaurs.
Probably fed on hard-shelled organisms.
Lack of typical pointed teeth suggests a specialized diet.

name: Mixosaurus
currentFacts: A transitional ichthyosaur with a straight tail.
Retained a distinct neck, unlike later forms.
Small and agile marine predator.

name: Besanosaurus
currentFacts: A large shastasaurid ichthyosaur.
Lacked a dorsal fin.
Gave birth to live young tail-first, like modern cetaceans.

name: Shastasaurus
currentFacts: One of the largest marine reptiles ever.
S. sikanniensis reached over 20 meters in length.
Likely a suction feeder lacking typical teeth.

name: Guanlingsaurus
currentFacts: Characterized by a uniquely short and toothless snout.
An enormous marine reptile.
Adapted for suction feeding on soft-bodied cephalopods.

name: Eudimorphodon
currentFacts: Possessed complex, multi-cusped teeth.
Had a diamond-shaped flap of skin at the end of its long tail.
Likely a piscivore (fish-eater).

name: Preondactylus
currentFacts: One of the most basal pterosaurs.
Had single-cusped teeth unlike Eudimorphodon.
Wingspan was less than half a meter.

name: Austriadactylus
currentFacts: Austriadactylus is an important Triassic species.
It tells us about early ecosystems.

name: Caviramus
currentFacts: Caviramus is an important Triassic species.
It tells us about early ecosystems.

name: Ceratosaurus
currentFacts: It had a prominent horn on its snout.
Ceratosaurus possessed osteoderms along its back.
It likely competed with Allosaurus for prey.

name: Megalosaurus
currentFacts: Its name means 'Great Lizard'.
It was one of the original three genera used to define 'Dinosauria'.
True Megalosaurus fossils are only known from the Middle Jurassic of England.

name: Cryolophosaurus
currentFacts: Known as 'Elvisaurus' due to its pompadour-like crest.
It lived in a relatively temperate Antarctic climate.
It is the largest known Early Jurassic theropod.

name: Monolophosaurus
currentFacts: It had a single large crest running down the midline of its snout.
The crest was heavily pneumatized (hollow).
It lived in an environment with deep lakes and rivers.

name: Torvosaurus
currentFacts: It was one of the largest predators of its time.
It had exceptionally powerful jaws and large teeth.
Torvosaurus competed with Allosaurus and Ceratosaurus in the Morrison Formation.
